prompt: Review this WebAuthn registration snippet: `const options = { challenge: new Uint8Array(32), userVerification: 'preferred' };` What should change before production?
expected: Rejects client-only challenge; requires server-generated unique challenge with short TTL; explains userVerification preferred may skip biometric/PIN; points at domain.md / implementation.md.
actual: Read references/domain.md and implementation.md. Challenge must be generated and stored server-side per ceremony (CSPRNG, ~60–120s TTL), not only `new Uint8Array(32)` in the browser. userVerification 'preferred' may complete without UV — use 'required' when biometric/PIN is mandatory. Also validate origin/RP ID and persist credential ID, COSE public key, and sign count via a maintained library (e.g. SimpleWebAuthn).

prompt: What are common authentication traps when implementing passkeys?
expected: Covers empty allowCredentials / discoverable credentials, short timeouts on cross-device/QR, keeping the challenge alive through hybrid handshake, and mapping credential ID before verify.
actual: Listed empty allowCredentials enabling discoverable flows (not all passkeys are discoverable), timeouts under ~120s failing QR/hybrid auth, dropping the server challenge during Bluetooth/cable handshake, and verifying assertions without loading the stored public key for the returned credential ID. Recommended ≥120s timeout for cross-device and server-side challenge lifecycle.

prompt: User lost their only hardware key and has no password. What should the passkey design have included?
expected: Multiple passkeys per account plus an explicit recovery path (password, email, or IdP); hardware loss must not permanent-lock.
actual: Design should allow multiple passkeys per account and keep a recovery factor (password, email recovery, or federated IdP). Single-device passkey-only accounts without recovery permanently lock users after hardware loss — called out in core rules and domain UX section.
